errors.description: The model completely misidentified the shapes and their attributes. The video explicitly shows a diamond, hexagon, pentagon, and square — none of which are rectangles or triangles. The model also hallucinated colors (green, gray, purple, red) not present in the ground truth description. This suggests the model either misperceived the visual input or generated plausible-sounding but entirely fabricated shape/color labels without grounding in the actual video content.

errors.evidence_quote: The green rectangle appears at the beginning... next shape appears at 0:02... gray hexagon appears at 0:02... next at 0:04... purple pentagon at 0:04... next at 0:06... red triangle at 0:06... video ends at 0:08
errors.description: The model assigned arbitrary, uniformly spaced timestamps (0:00, 0:02, 0:04, 0:06, 0:08) that do not match the actual drawing durations provided in the scene description. This indicates the model either failed to perceive the actual timing cues in the video or invented a regular 2-second interval pattern as a heuristic, ignoring the irregular and explicitly defined durations (0.6s, 2.8s, 2.4s, 2.2s).

errors.evidence_quote: It remains on the screen until the next shape appears... Therefore, the duration... is from X to Y
errors.description: The model assumed that the 'duration' of a shape is the time it remains visible on screen until the next shape appears — which is incorrect. The question explicitly asks for the 'duration of drawing' (i.e., the time taken to draw each shape), not the time it remains displayed. The model misinterpreted the task goal, conflating display duration with drawing duration, leading to a fundamentally wrong premise.

Based on its incorrect timestamp assignments and wrong premise, the model calculated all durations as exactly 2.0 seconds, ignoring the actual durations provided in the scene description. This is not an arithmetic error per se, but a misuse of quantitative data — applying a uniform value derived from a flawed temporal model rather than using the actual observed or provided durations.

analysis_result.analysis: The model failed catastrophically on multiple fronts. It hallucinated the shapes and colors entirely, misinterpreted the task goal (confusing display duration with drawing duration), assigned arbitrary and incorrect timestamps, and produced uniformly wrong numerical outputs. The root cause appears to be a fundamental failure in visual perception and task comprehension, leading to a cascade of errors grounded in fabricated assumptions rather than the actual video content. No part of the model's reasoning aligns with the ground truth, indicating a severe breakdown in both perception and logical inference.
